findings.title: Negative offset to QuerySet slicing will crash at the database
findings.body: Inside `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (a negative integer). The Django QuerySet `__getitem__` does not support a negative `start` in a slice: `Query.set_limits` forwards the negative value as the SQL `OFFSET`, which PostgreSQL rejects with a syntax error (e.g. `OFFSET -100`). The claim in the comment that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' is false. Any superuser / global-access caller who supplies a cursor with a negative offset through `?optimized_pagination=true` on `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` will get a 500 instead of pagination.

findings.title: `BasePaginator.get_result` silently changes behavior for every paginator subclass
findings.body: The diff modifies `BasePaginator.get_result` (used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and any other subclass) from `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` followed by `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. This is not localized to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`; it changes the contract for every existing paginator. The 'Performance optimization' comment is misleading: this is a defensive clamp, not an optimization. The change is also inconsistent - negative offsets are only clamped for forward (`is_prev=False`) cursors; backward cursors still pass negative offsets straight to `queryset[offset:stop]`, which has the same crash potential. The behavior change should be scoped to the new paginator and either documented or rejected with a `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: `enable_advanced_features` is gated to admins but provides no functional benefit
findings.body: The only behavioral difference between `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `BasePaginator` (when `enable_advanced_features=True`) is the negative-offset branch, which crashes Django (see other finding). The endpoint hard-codes `enable_advanced_features=True` whenever `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. So the entire feature shipped behind admin-only access is non-functional, while still adding ~100 lines of duplicated code, an `optimized_pagination` query-string toggle, and a new exported class. The PR should either implement what the comments describe or be reduced to a no-op flag until a real implementation exists.

findings.title: No tests added for `OptimizedCursorPaginator`
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class and the modified `BasePaginator.get_result` slicing behavior have no accompanying tests. Cursor-based pagination in this file is subtle (extra row fetching, prev-direction reversal, `cursor.value` dedup, `offset + limit + extra` length check), and the PR introduces a new code path (`enable_advanced_features=True`) plus a behavioral change to the shared `BasePaginator.get_result`. At minimum, tests should cover: (1) forward pagination with the new clamp, (2) backward pagination with positive and negative offsets, (3) the `enable_advanced_features=True` branch with both negative and non-negative offsets, (4) the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` post-filter path when `offset` is negative.

findings.title: Pre-existing typo `queryset.query.order_b` is one line from the changed code
findings.body: On the unchanged line 105 of `BasePaginator.build_queryset`, the assignment reads `queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by)` instead of `queryset.query.order_by = tuple(new_order_by)`. This is a typo that would raise `AttributeError: 'Query' object has no attribute 'order_b'` whenever the code path is reached (DESC ordering on a queryset that already has `-%s` in its order_by and `asc=True`). The PR is touching the very same `BasePaginator.get_result` / pagination file; the typo should be fixed in this PR while the area is being modified, since the bug is reachable and would be exercised by anything that pre-applies `-datetime` and then pages forward via `cursor.is_prev=False`.

findings.title: Docstring and inline comments overstate and misrepresent the feature
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` docstring claims 'Negative offset support for efficient reverse pagination', 'Streamlined boundary condition handling', 'Optimized query path for large datasets'. The `BasePaginator.get_result` comment claims 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` claims 'permissions are checked at the queryset level'. None of these are true: Django ORM does not silently fix a negative slice (it produces `OFFSET -100` which the DB rejects), no queryset-level permission filter is added in the new code, and no query path is actually optimized. The comments also justify the negative-offset branch with 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds', which would be a security/authorization concern if it actually worked. The comments must be rewritten to match what the code does.
